ratingCriteria.0: Asymptomatic but with documented sleep disorder breathing
ratingCriteria.50: Requires use of breathing assistance device such as CPAP
ratingCriteria.100: Chronic respiratory failure with carbon dioxide retention, cor pulmonale, or requires tracheostomy

commonDenialReasons.reason: No diagnosis during active duty service
commonDenialReasons.counterStrategy: Establish nexus through weight gain, respiratory conditions, or PTSD connection

commonDenialReasons.reason: No nexus opinion linking to service or service-connected condition
commonDenialReasons.counterStrategy: Obtain IMO addressing secondary connection or aggravation

commonDenialReasons.reason: Weight gain after service attributed to natural causes
commonDenialReasons.counterStrategy: Document medication side effects, limited mobility from SC conditions

in_service_symptoms.description: Evidence of snoring, fatigue, or breathing issues during service

weight_history.description: Weight changes and their relationship to service/SC conditions

successPatterns.pattern: Secondary to PTSD with supporting IMO
successPatterns.description: Sleep apnea claimed secondary to PTSD with medical opinion discussing sleep architecture disruption

successPatterns.pattern: Secondary to sinusitis/rhinitis with anatomical evidence
successPatterns.description: When nasal/sinus conditions already SC and contribute to airway obstruction
Compelling lay evidence from service roommates/spouses about observed symptoms

failurePatterns.description: Direct service connection claims rarely succeed without STR documentation
failurePatterns.mitigation: Reframe as secondary claim to established SC condition

failurePatterns.pattern: Weight-based argument without SC condition link
failurePatterns.description: Claiming weight gain caused sleep apnea without connecting weight gain to service
failurePatterns.mitigation: Document how SC conditions limit physical activity or cause weight gain

commonFactors: Significant post-service weight gain without connection to service
